title: The Lion King
wiki_lead:
The Lion King is a 1994 American animated musical drama film directed by Roger Allers and Rob Minkoff and written by Irene Mecchi, Jonathan Roberts, and Linda Woolverton. Produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation, it features an ensemble voice cast consisting of Matthew Broderick, James Earl Jones, Jeremy Irons, Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Moira Kelly, Niketa Calame, Madge Sinclair, Nathan Lane, Ernie Sabella, Whoopi Goldberg, Cheech Marin, Rowan Atkinson, and Robert Guillaume. The story follows a young lion prince named Simba, who is exiled from his kingdom after his father, King Mufasa, is murdered by his uncle Scar, who usurps the throne. As he grows up, Simba must decide whether to return to his homeland to confront Scar and reclaim his rightful place as king.
The Lion King was conceived during conversations among various Disney executives, to whom several writers submitted early treatments under the title King of the Jungle. Original director George Scribner had envisioned The Lion King as a nature documentary-style film, with Allers joining as co-director. The Lion King's plot draws inspiration from several sources, notably Bambi (1942), William Shakespeare's play Hamlet, as well as the Bible. Woolverton, the screenwriter for Disney's Beauty and the Beast (1991), drafted early scripts for The Lion King before Mecchi and Roberts were hired to revise once Woolverton left to prioritize other projects. Scribner departed due to disagreements over the studio's decision to reimagine the film as a musical, with original songs by Elton John and Tim Rice. Minkoff was hired to replace him in April 1992. Throughout production, the creative team visited Kenya for research and inspiration.
Released in theaters on June 24, 1994 by Walt Disney Pictures, The Lion King was praised by critics for its music, story, themes, and animation. With an initial worldwide gross of $763 million, it completed its theatrical run as the highest-grossing film of 1994 and the second-highest-grossing film of all time, behind Jurassic Park (1993). It held the title of highest-grossing animated film until it was replaced by Finding Nemo in 2003. The film remains the highest-grossing traditionally animated film of all time. The film was also the best-selling film on home video, having sold over 55 million copies worldwide. It won two Academy Awards, as well as the Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy.
The success of the film launched a multibillion-dollar franchise comprising a Broadway adaptation, two direct-to-video follow-ups, two television series, and a photorealistic remake (which itself spawned a prequel), which in 2019 also became the highest-grossing animated film at the time of its release. In 2016, The Lion King was selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry by the Library of Congress as being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant".

grok_lead: The Lion King is a 1994 American animated musical film produced by Walt Disney Feature Animation and released by Walt Disney Pictures, directed by Roger Allers and Rob Minkoff. The story centers on Simba, a lion cub and heir to the Pride Lands throne, who is tricked by his uncle Scar into believing he caused the death of his father, King Mufasa; after fleeing in guilt, Simba matures in exile with companions Timon and Pumbaa before returning to confront Scar and restore balance to the kingdom. Featuring songs composed by Elton John and Tim Rice with score by Hans Zimmer, the film premiered in the United States on June 15, 1994, and achieved widespread commercial success, grossing $968.5 million worldwide during its initial run and becoming the highest-grossing film of 1994 as well as the second-highest-grossing film of all time at release. It received critical acclaim for its animation, voice performances by actors including James Earl Jones as Mufasa and Jeremy Irons as Scar, and emotional storytelling, earning two Academy Awards for Best Original Score and Best Original Song ("Can You Feel the Love Tonight"). The film's narrative draws from diverse influences including Shakespeare's Hamlet, ancient Egyptian mythology, and African folklore, though debates persist over similarities to the 1960s Japanese anime Kimba the White Lion, which Disney has attributed to shared archetypal themes rather than direct copying. The success of the film spawned a multimedia franchise encompassing direct-to-video sequels like The Lion King II: Simba's Pride (1998) and The Lion King 1Â½ (2004), a long-running Broadway musical adaptation that premiered in 1997 under director Julie Taymor and has grossed over $9 billion worldwide as the highest-earning stage production in history, a 2019 photorealistic remake directed by Jon Favreau that earned $1.66 billion, and the 2024 prequel Mufasa: The Lion King. The franchise has collectively generated billions in revenue across film, theater, merchandise, and theme park attractions, cementing The Lion King as a cornerstone of Disney's cultural and financial empire.
